thread:
maria_support: Filing an escalation for ACME / atlas-app. Their dedicated pool dp-7 started spiking 429s and token tail latencies around 11:10 PDT. They mention repeated cache evictions and auth retry storms. Posting initial details.

devon_infra: can you share tenant id, qps, and whether it's sustained or a brief burst?

maria_support: tenant=acct-atlas-42, baseline ~120 qps with bursts up to ~300 qps for ~5m. They enabled a new feature that sends very long contexts (~100k-130k tokens).

oliver_oncall: noted. In previous incidents long-context sessions tend to create very large KV entries and cause slab fragmentation -> eviction waves. Can we pull kvcache metrics (hits/misses/evict rate) and alloc failure logs? :eyes:

maria_support: attaching the customer's curl they used to repro: 

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-13b","input":"<~120k tokens>"}'
```

maria_support: customer logs show many 429s plus repeated cache_miss / evict_success entries.

devon_infra: quick observability check: dp-7 kvcache_evictions/s jumped from ~12 -> ~900 at 11:09 and stayed elevated ~15-20m. We see slab_realloc failures and more compaction events; total mem not maxed but fragmentation high.

oliver_oncall: autoscaler behavior? did dp-7 scale out when load increased?

devon_infra: autoscale-bot: "Autoscaler: dp-7 attempted scale; pool at configured max_nodes=6; no additional nodes provisioned."

autoscale-bot: pool hit reservation cap during incident window.

jess_prodeng: customer-facing question: do they have burst capacity in contract? If not, might need to offer a temporary increase. But root cause first.

oliver_oncall: @devon_infra please paste a small sample of kvcache traces and key size distribution. Looking for oversized per-session frames or hot keys.

devon_infra: sample logs (redacted):

```
[11:08:52] kvcache: put key=ctx:acct-atlas-42:sess:846201 size=489600
[11:08:55] kvcache: put key=ctx:acct-atlas-42:sess:846202 size=503424
[11:09:05] kvcache: fail_realloc slab=4 want=600k got=64k
[11:09:09] kvcache: evict key=ctx:acct-atlas-42:sess:801234 reason=fragmentation
[11:09:30] kvcache: evict_many count=312
```

devon_infra: per-entry sizes ~450-500KB. Long contexts are being stored as single large frames which makes slab reuse hard and causes fragmentation.

maria_support: ACME wants an immediate mitigation. They'll consider rolling back, but they'd prefer a quick config change to stop 429s.

oliver_oncall: short-term mitigations we can take:
- enforce a per-tenant max KV entry size and reject larger requests at the edge (fast)
- route tenant traffic to an overflow pool with larger reservation (if available)
- run slab compaction on dp-7 to reduce fragmentation (maintenance)

oliver_oncall: propose: apply a per-tenant kv-entry cap of 128KB on acct-atlas-42 and return a 413-like error for oversize contexts. Who can roll this gate?

devon_infra: I can push an edge rule, but need customer approval for returning 413. Alternatively we can redirect them to a helper pool.

maria_support: pinged customer; they replied: "OK to return 413 for oversized requests; we'll revert if needed." They gave green light.

devon_infra: deploying gateway rule: tenant=acct-atlas-42 max_kv_entry_size=131072 on dp-7-edge. Oversize requests will get 413 + context_too_large. Monitoring now.

devon_infra: after rule, eviction/saturation metrics dropped — evictions/s down to ~20 and 429s subsided. Token-latency tail improved but still slightly elevated.

eng-runtime-bot: scheduled slab compaction on dp-7 at 11:40 PDT. Estimated ~90s for background compaction and minor IO.

oliver_oncall: while compaction runs, capture heap snapshot and run post-compaction histograms to confirm fragmentation reduced. Also open an incident ticket for follow-ups.

sre-bot: Incident INC-2025 created (priority=P2)  follow KV pressure playbook and assign eng-runtime + infra.

jess_prodeng: follow-ups to track: product to define per-tenant long-context policy and opt-in for burst; runtime to explore streaming/sharded KV entries for long contexts; infra to add soft overflow/auto-burst when pool hits max_nodes.

maria_support: ACME confirmed 429s are gone; they will coordinate a controlled rollout of the long-context feature with our recommendations. Closing Slack escalation; ticket remains open for engineering follow-ups. :white_check_mark:

oliver_oncall: thanks all. We'll keep the incident open for the RFCs and a potential dedicated fix. If ACME wants immediate permanent relief we can offer a larger reservation or temporary burst increase.

maria_support: noted, I'll follow up with ACME next week and add docs for recommended limits in Dedicated pools.
